page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9i.large is an entry-tier instance within the compute-optimized family, deployed on KVM virtualization. The instance provides 2 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The compute resources are paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core, standard for compute-centric workloads.

The hardware configuration does not include local storage, meaning all persistent data and operating system installations rely entirely on network-attached storage. GPU acceleration is not present, and the server includes a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The dedicated vCPU allocation ensures steady execution without performance throttling or resource contention typical of burstable instances. The 1:2 memory allocation is cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that do not justify larger, more expensive RAM allocations. However, total memory capacity and the absence of high-speed local disk storage represent distinct tradeoffs for data-intensive processing.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9i.large is suited for workloads such as front-end web serving, application middleware, microservices, continuous integration build runners, and lightweight computational pipelines.
